explanation: Template template parameters allow a class or function template to accept other class templates as arguments. This feature enables highly flexible and generic code by parameterizing over templates themselves, rather than just types or values. It is particularly useful when designing template classes that depend on other template classes, facilitating advanced metaprogramming and code reuse in modern C++.
code_example: static void display() { std::cout << "Inner template with type" << std::endl; }
example_explanation: This example defines a class template 'Outer' that takes a template template parameter 'T', which itself is a class template accepting a type parameter. The 'Inner' template struct is passed as an argument to 'Outer', demonstrating how template template parameters enable 'Outer' to work with any compatible template class. The 'call' method invokes a static function within the 'Inner' template instantiated with 'int', showcasing the flexibility and power of template template parameters in modern C++ metaprogramming.
